main_body: A church pew seen from the side/end: a tall wooden backrest plank on the left and a seat/front panel on the right with three red cushion panels drawn flat on the face
top_band: Brown band rows 14-15 (2 rows, L=124) at the top of the seat panel, directly under a dark outline; it is no different in kind from the rim, and the red cushion panels below are vertical faces
evidence: In the column at x=8 the scan shows only a 2-row light brown strip (rows 14-15), followed by red panels (rows 16-26, 30-40, 44-54) separated by brown bars. Those panels are vertical faces. No seat surface is visible from above; the seat is only a 2px rim. The tall left plank is a flat backrest strip seen edge-on. It reads as a front/side elevation with a thin cap line, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile for the references. Its flat-fill coverage is 25%, against 0-13%. The red panels and brown plank are large flat areas with no grain, dots or highlights. The outline is a tinted dark brown (2% neutral), so it is not a sticker line, but the material ramps are only 2-3 steps, which is much shallower than the references.
